Stratified Generalized Linear Models

Source: R/stratified_glm.R
stratified_glm.Rd

This modeling approach subdivides the majority class into strata of size of the minority class, times a ratio (which is 1 by default). The models are combined using the same technique for combining multiple imputed data sets in order to not decrease standard error estimates with artificially large sample sizes. See stratified_glm vignette for more details.

Usage

stratified_glm(
  formula,
  data,
  ratio = 1,
  family = stats::binomial(link = "logit"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'stratified.glm'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'stratified.glm'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'stratified.glm'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'stratified.glm'
plot(x, geom = ggplot2::geom_density(alpha = 0.5), facet = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

formula

an object of class "formula" (or one that can be coerced to that class): a symbolic description of the model to be fitted. See [stats::glm()] for more information.

data

an optional data frame, list or environment (or object coercible by as.data.frame to a data frame) containing the variables in the model. See [stats::glm()] for more information.

ratio

the ratio of the small-to-large group. That is, how many observations from the larger group should be randomly selected. A ratio of 1 means that there are the (approximately) same number of observations in both outcome groups.

family

a description of the error distribution and link function to be used in the model. This should almost always be `binomial(link='logit')`.

...

currently not used.

object

results from `stratified_glm()`.

newdata

optionally, a data frame in which to look for variables with which to predict. If omitted, the fitted linear predictors are used.

x

results from `stratified_glm()`

geom

the `ggplot2` geometry to use. Typically [ggplot2::geom_density()] or [ggplot2::geom_histogram()].

facet

whether to use [ggplot2::facet_wrap()] based on the model type.

Value

a list object with the following elements:

formula

an object of class "formula" (or one that can be coerced to that class): a symbolic description of the model to be fitted.

data

data frame used for the model fitting.

ratio

the ratio used for the big to small group.

cont_tab

the contingency table for the outcome variable.

data_big

subset of `data` for the bigger of the two groups.

data_small

subset of `data` for the larger of the two groups.

model

the [stats::glm()] results using all the data.

n_models

the number of models that will be estimated.

assignment

a numeric vector equal to `nrow(data)` that corresponds to what.

models

a list with the following elements for each model run:

model

the results of [stats::glm()].

data

the subset of `data` used for this iteration.

fitted

the fitted values for this iteration. Note that the order of this vector corresponds to the `data` subset for this iteration, not the full data.

rows

an integer vector mapping the rows from this iteration back to the full data frame.

fitted

matrix of fitted values. The columns correspond to each model iteration.

the results from [mitools::MIcombine()].

a numeric vector with the fitted values. Note that for the small group, the fitted value is the average across all models. Individual vectors of fitted values can be retrieved from `object$fitted`.

a `ggplot2` expression.
